title: Auckland's Diwali Festival Returns October 31 With Fireworks, Sky Tower Lights
excerpt: The free BNZ Auckland Diwali Festival takes over Aotea Square and Queen Street on October 31 and November 1, with the Sky Tower lit from October 23 and Sunday fireworks at 8:50pm.
body:
• The BNZ Auckland Diwali Festival returns to central Auckland on Saturday, October 31 and Sunday, November 1, 2026 — free entry, midday to 9pm Saturday and 9:10pm Sunday.
  • The festival takes over Aotea Square, Queen Street and Rutland Street with music, dance, workshops and vegetarian food stalls; Sunday closes with fireworks at about 8:50pm.
  • Auckland's Sky Tower is lit for Diwali from October 23 to November 2, and the new Te Waihorotiu Station on the City Rail Link drops visitors a three-minute walk from Aotea Square.
  • First held in 2002, the festival draws more than 65,000 people a year and is one of the largest Diwali celebrations in the Southern Hemisphere — plan transport and arrive before dark for the lights.

Auckland's city centre will close out Diwali season with its biggest celebration of the year. The BNZ Auckland Diwali Festival returns on Saturday, October 31 and Sunday, November 1, 2026, filling Aotea Square, Queen Street and Rutland Street with free music, dance, art, workshops and family activities, alongside vegetarian food stalls. Auckland Council's festival announcement confirms the hours: midday to 9pm on Saturday and midday to 9:10pm on Sunday.

What is on

Traditional and contemporary Indian performances run across multiple stages through both days, with exhibitions, hands-on workshops and activities for the whole family. Food is central: the festival is New Zealand's largest vegetarian festival, and all 2026 stalls serve vegetarian dishes made without eggs — pakora, pav bhaji and kulfi among the staples listed by AucklandNZ, the city's official visitor site. The weekend ends with a public fireworks display on Sunday at about 8:50pm.

The celebration starts before the festival weekend. Auckland's Sky Tower, the 328-metre landmark at the corner of Victoria and Federal Streets, is illuminated for Diwali from October 23 through November 2, giving the city a week-long marker visible well beyond the festival streets.

"Diwali has always been a joyful time when families and communities come together. That same sense of connection is at the heart of the BNZ Auckland Diwali Festival."

— Arnav Taode, Festival Event Manager, Tataki Auckland Unlimited

A festival that has run since 2002

First held in 2002, the Auckland Diwali Festival has become a fixture of the city's cultural calendar and one of the largest Diwali celebrations in the Southern Hemisphere, drawing more than 65,000 people each year. It honours Diwali — also known as Deepavali — and its message of light over darkness, good over evil and knowledge over ignorance. BNZ Chief Executive Dan Huggins has described the festival as an important fixture on Auckland's cultural calendar since its launch.

"Auckland's Indian communities have many different traditions and ways of celebrating Diwali, and the festival gives them a platform to share their culture with all of Tamaki Makaurau," Taode said.

Getting there

This year's festival is among the first major city-centre events served by Auckland's new City Rail Link. Te Waihorotiu Station, next to Aotea Square, is a three-minute walk from the festival site; the Downtown Ferry Terminal is about a 15-minute walk. Entry is free, with food available for purchase. Full programme details are on the official festival page and the Heart of the City listing. For Indian families visiting New Zealand in late October, the festival weekend is the natural anchor for an Auckland stay: arrive for the Sky Tower lighting in the preceding week, and stay through Sunday night's fireworks.
